questions.Question: What best describes diabetes mellitus?
questions.A: A syndrome characterized by hyperglycemia and disturbances of carbohydrate, fat and protein metabolism
questions.B: An acute infection of the pancreas
questions.C: A disorder limited to fat metabolism
questions.D: A condition caused only by excess dietary sugar

questions.Question: Which major physiological defect is involved in diabetes mellitus?
questions.A: Defects in insulin secretion, insulin action, or both
questions.D: Excess growth hormone in every patient

questions.Question: Which of the following is classified as Type 1 diabetes mellitus?
Type 2 diabetes mellitus is characterized by which combination?
questions.A: Insulin resistance with a progressive insulin secretory defect
questions.B: Absolute insulin excess with no insulin resistance

questions.Question: Which is an example of a genetic defect of beta-cell function listed in the material?
Which condition is listed as an endocrine cause of other specific types of diabetes?
Which drug is given as an example of drug/chemical-induced diabetes?
Which infection is listed as a cause of a specific type of diabetes?

questions.D: It becomes completely independent of insulin resistance

questions.Question: According to the material, beta-cell function at diagnosis of Type 2 diabetes may already be compromised by approximately:
Which is a major goal of diabetes care?
questions.A: Prevention of acute and chronic complications

questions.Question: What is an important goal of diabetes management regarding self-care?
questions.A: Promotion of self-management practices and empowerment

questions.Question: At first contact, an important step is to:
questions.A: Attempt to correctly classify the diabetes
questions.D: Assume every patient has Type 1 diabetes

questions.Question: Which assessment helps identify complications of diabetes?
Why can classification of diabetes type sometimes be difficult?
Which laboratory measurement may help facilitate classification of diabetes type?
What is the role of immune markers in some diabetes classifications?
questions.A: They may help identify immune-mediated beta-cell destruction

questions.Question: Which approach is associated with the best results in diabetes management?
What role should the person with diabetes assume?
questions.A: An active role in care and self-management
questions.D: A role limited to taking antibiotics

questions.Question: Which group of conditions is commonly associated with diabetes?
Why is persistent hyperglycemia important in diabetes management?
questions.A: It is harmful and contributes to complications
questions.D: It eliminates the need for treatment

questions.Question: What is the main glycemic management objective?
questions.A: Achieve and maintain glycemic control as close to target as safely possible
questions.D: Use insulin in every patient immediately

questions.Question: Which metabolic stage may precede diabetes mellitus?
questions.A: Impaired glucose tolerance and/or impaired fasting glycemia

questions.Question: What BMI target is listed for metabolic control?
What is the listed blood pressure target for metabolic control?
How often should HbA1c generally be reviewed in routine follow-up according to the material?
What does HbA1c primarily reflect?
questions.A: Average blood glucose over approximately 2–3 months
questions.B: Blood glucose from the previous hour only

questions.A: It does not measure glycemic variability or hypoglycemia

questions.Question: For patients with marked glycemic variability, control is best judged using:
What is an important purpose of self-monitoring of blood glucose?
questions.A: To observe readings, patterns and trends and take appropriate action

questions.Question: Continuous glucose monitors measure glucose in:
Continuous glucose monitors may provide alarms when glucose is:
questions.A: Too high, too low, or changing rapidly

questions.Question: CGM is particularly useful as a supplemental tool for patients with:
questions.A: Hypoglycemia unawareness or frequent hypoglycemic episodes

questions.Question: Which is a foundation of diabetes care?
Which lifestyle intervention is recommended for overweight or obese persons with diabetes?
Which dietary principle is emphasized for people with diabetes?
questions.A: A healthy, balanced diet individualized to the patient's circumstances
questions.B: A single identical diet for everyone
questions.D: Diet based only on expensive foods

questions.Question: Dietary planning should consider the patient's:
questions.A: Eating habits, lifestyle, culture and financial circumstances

questions.Question: For Type 2 diabetes, which dietary measure is described as especially important?
Which type of carbohydrate is especially encouraged in the Type 2 dietary considerations?
What is an important consideration when prescribing physical activity for Type 1 diabetes?
questions.A: Education about the effect of exercise on blood glucose

questions.Question: Rigorous exercise lasting more than 30 minutes may predispose insulin-requiring patients to:
For Type 2 diabetes, structured exercise training of more than 150 minutes per week is associated with:
Which type of training is recommended at least twice weekly when there are no contraindications?
Why should exercise be individualized?
questions.A: Age, previous activity level and comorbidities should be considered
questions.B: Every patient has identical exercise capacity

questions.Question: What can heavy alcohol intake do in diabetes?
questions.A: Worsen glycemic/metabolic control and increase hypoglycemia risk
questions.D: Improve insulin secretion in every patient

questions.Question: Which lifestyle intervention is specifically recommended?
Which pharmacologic therapy is used in both Type 1 and Type 2 diabetes?
Which class of medication is described as oral glucose-lowering therapy for Type 2 diabetes?
Which drug is a second-generation sulfonylurea?
What is the pancreatic action of sulfonylureas?
questions.A: They augment insulin secretion by acting on ATP-dependent potassium channels

questions.Question: Which drug is a non-sulfonylurea secretagogue?
How is repaglinide typically timed in relation to meals?
questions.D: Only at bedtime regardless of meals

questions.Question: What is a major action of metformin?
questions.A: Improves peripheral insulin sensitivity and decreases hepatic glucose output

questions.Question: Which drug class delays carbohydrate absorption in the gut?
Which is an example of an alpha-glucosidase inhibitor?
What is the main action of thiazolidinediones?
Which is an example of a thiazolidinedione?
What does GLP-1 do after food intake?
Which is an effect of incretins described in the material?
questions.A: They suppress glucagon release and delay gastric emptying

questions.Question: Which drug is a GLP-1 analogue described in the material?
What is a characteristic of sitagliptin?
questions.A: It inhibits the enzyme that degrades GLP-1

questions.Question: What is amylin co-secreted with?
What is pramlintide?
questions.A: An amylin analogue administered subcutaneously before meals

questions.Question: What is the main role of basal insulin?
questions.A: Provide relatively uniform insulin coverage throughout day and night

questions.Question: What is the main role of prandial insulin?
Which insulin has an onset of approximately 5–15 minutes?
Which insulin has an onset of approximately 30–60 minutes?
Which insulin has an effective duration of approximately 10–16 hours in the material?
Which insulin is described as long-acting and peakless?
What is the approximate effective duration of insulin glargine in the material?
Type 1 diabetes generally requires:
What total daily insulin dose is suggested for initiating Type 1 diabetes therapy in the material?
Which regimen is recommended for most people with Type 1 diabetes?
questions.A: Multiple daily injections or continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion

questions.Question: Prandial insulin dosing in Type 1 diabetes should consider:
questions.A: Carbohydrate intake, premeal glucose and anticipated activity

questions.Question: What is one advantage of an insulin pump?
questions.A: It provides flexible insulin delivery closer to physiological patterns
questions.B: It eliminates the need for glucose monitoring

questions.Question: What does a closed-loop system combine?
questions.A: CGM data with an insulin infusion pump

questions.Question: A patient with diabetes asks why regular follow-up is necessary even when feeling well. What is the best response based on the material?
questions.A: Diabetes is lifelong and requires continuing care to prevent complications
questions.B: Follow-up is needed only when symptoms occur

questions.Question: A patient newly diagnosed with diabetes cannot clearly be classified as Type 1 or Type 2. What is an appropriate approach?
questions.A: Use clinical judgment, history, presentation and selective laboratory testing
questions.D: Avoid follow-up until classification is perfect

questions.Question: A patient has an uncertain diabetes classification. Which test may help clarify beta-cell function?
A patient with stable glycemic control has consistently met treatment goals. How often should HbA1c be performed at minimum according to the material?
A patient has recently had diabetes therapy changed and is not meeting glycemic goals. Which HbA1c schedule is most appropriate according to the material?
questions.D: Only at the next emergency visit

questions.Question: A patient with diabetes has hemolytic anemia and an HbA1c result that does not fit the clinical picture. What should the clinician recognize?
questions.A: HbA1c may be unreliable because of abnormal red blood cell turnover
questions.C: The patient must have Type 1 diabetes

questions.Question: A patient has frequent hypoglycemic episodes and is unable to recognize warning symptoms. Which technology may be particularly useful?
A patient uses SMBG but records readings without interpreting patterns. What education is needed?
questions.A: Understand readings, patterns and trends and take appropriate action

questions.Question: A patient with Type 1 diabetes plans vigorous exercise for more than 30 minutes. What is a key teaching point?
questions.A: Exercise can predispose to hypoglycemia, so appropriate preventive measures are needed

questions.Question: A sedentary patient with Type 2 diabetes wants to begin exercise. What is an appropriate recommendation?
questions.A: Encourage regular exercise and reduce sedentary time
questions.C: Avoid resistance training in all cases

questions.Question: A patient with Type 2 diabetes asks what type of carbohydrate is preferable. What answer best follows the material?
questions.D: Candy as the main carbohydrate source

questions.Question: A patient says a diabetes diet is too expensive. What principle should guide the dietary plan?
questions.A: Use foods within the patient's cultural milieu and financial reach
questions.D: Use the same diet for every patient

questions.Question: A patient with Type 2 diabetes has severe hyperglycemia with random glucose of 330 mg/dL and weight loss. What therapy should be strongly considered?
A newly diagnosed Type 2 diabetic patient has HbA1c of 11% with ketosis. Which approach is supported by the material?
questions.A: Consider insulin because of severe hyperglycemia and catabolic features

questions.Question: A patient with Type 2 diabetes is started on basal insulin. What is the typical initiating dose described?
A patient taking basal insulin has acceptable fasting glucose but HbA1c remains above target. What is a reasonable next step described in the material?
A patient with Type 1 diabetes asks whether insulin can eventually be stopped after good control. What should the nurse explain based on the material?
questions.A: Type 1 diabetes requires lifelong insulin therapy
questions.B: Insulin is needed for only one month
questions.C: Insulin can always be replaced by diet
questions.D: Insulin is never needed after diagnosis

questions.Question: A patient with Type 1 diabetes is learning to adjust mealtime insulin. Which information should be considered?
questions.A: Carbohydrate intake, premeal blood glucose and anticipated activity

questions.Question: A patient asks about the purpose of basal insulin. Which explanation is correct?
questions.A: It provides relatively uniform insulin coverage through day and night

questions.Question: A patient asks why prandial insulin is given around meals. What is the best explanation?
A patient using regular insulin wants to know when it begins acting. According to the material, the approximate onset is:
A patient using insulin glargine asks about its duration. Which range is listed?
A patient with Type 2 diabetes refuses insulin because they believe it means they have failed. What communication is most appropriate?
questions.A: Explain that Type 2 diabetes is progressive and insulin may eventually be indicated; it is not a punishment
questions.B: Tell the patient insulin is a punishment

questions.Question: A patient with Type 2 diabetes needs a new glucose-lowering medication. Which approach best fits the material?
questions.A: Individualize the choice using efficacy, cost, side effects, weight, comorbidities and hypoglycemia risk

questions.Question: A patient with diabetes has cardiovascular disease. Which broader management strategy is appropriate?
questions.A: Address glycemia, BP, lipids, weight and other cardiovascular risk factors

questions.Question: A 45-year-old patient with Type 2 diabetes has cardiovascular disease. What lipid-lowering therapy is specifically discussed?
A patient with diabetes asks why the feet are examined regularly. Which principle supports this?
questions.A: Screening for vascular complications and the diabetic foot is an essential part of care
questions.B: Foot assessment is unrelated to diabetes
questions.D: Foot assessment is needed only after amputation

questions.Question: A patient with diabetes has no current symptoms of complications. What is the appropriate approach?
questions.A: Continue scheduled screening and preventive care

questions.Question: A patient asks what 'look left' means in the diabetes reminder from the material. What should the nurse say?
A patient asks what 'look right' means in the diabetes reminder. What is the best answer?
questions.A: Glycemic, blood pressure and lipid targets

questions.Question: A patient asks what 'look inward' means in the diabetes reminder. What does it emphasize?
A diabetes clinic lacks adequate monitoring equipment and trained staff. Which improvement best follows the material?
questions.A: Provide appropriately trained staff, diagnostic/monitoring equipment and access to medications

questions.Question: A patient with Type 2 diabetes wants to prevent progression because they are at high risk. Which intervention has evidence in the material?
questions.A: Dietary modification, regular physical activity and modest weight loss

questions.Question: A patient with Type 2 diabetes asks whether physical activity can improve HbA1c. What is the best response?
questions.A: Yes, physical activity can help lower HbA1c, especially with dietary modification
questions.B: No, exercise has no metabolic effect

questions.Question: A patient with diabetes consumes heavy amounts of alcohol. What risk should be discussed?
questions.A: Worsened glycemic/metabolic control and increased risk of hypoglycemia
questions.C: Improved glycemic control in all cases

questions.Question: A patient with Type 2 diabetes has obesity and cannot achieve recommended treatment targets with medical therapy. What additional option is discussed for carefully selected patients?
A patient with diabetes asks why lifestyle change remains important after starting medication. What is the best explanation?
questions.A: Lifestyle measures are foundational components of diabetes care and support glycemic and cardiovascular risk reduction
questions.C: Lifestyle has no effect on diabetes
questions.D: Exercise should always be stopped after medication

questions.Question: A patient with frequent glucose fluctuations has an acceptable HbA1c but recurrent hypoglycemia. Which statement best reflects the material?
questions.A: HbA1c alone does not capture hypoglycemia or glycemic variability, so SMBG should also be considered

questions.Question: A patient with Type 2 diabetes is beginning pharmacologic therapy. What is the key overarching aim?
questions.A: Achieve desired HbA1c while minimizing side effects and considering patient factors

questions.Question: A patient with diabetes asks whether care should focus only on blood glucose. What is the best response?
questions.A: No; diabetes management also includes cardiovascular risk reduction and screening for complications
questions.B: Yes; glucose is the only concern
